addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

addedBlocks:
## npx
NotebookLM MCP - Access NotebookLM (notebooklm.google.com).

**Auth:** If you get authentication errors, run `nlm login` via your Bash/terminal tool. This is the automated authentication method that handles everything. Only use save_auth_tokens as a fallback if the CLI fails.
**Account Switching:** To switch Google Accounts for the MCP server, run `nlm login switch <profile>` in Bash. The MCP server instantly uses the active default profile.
**Confirmation:** Tools with confirm param require user approval before setting confirm=True.
**Studio:** After creating audio/video/infographic/slides, poll studio_status for completion.

Consolidated tools:
- source_add(source_type=url|text|drive|file, url=..., document_id=..., text=..., file_path=...): Add any source type
- studio_create(artifact_type=audio|video|...): Create any artifact type
- studio_revise: Revise individual slides in an existing slide deck
- download_artifact(artifact_type=audio|video|...): Download any artifact type
- note_create/note_list/note_update/note_delete: Manage notes in notebooks

attachment.content:
- paseo: Paseo reference for managing agents and worktrees. Load whenever you need to create agents, send them prompts, or manage worktrees.
- paseo-advisor: Spin up a single agent as an advisor — second opinion on the current task. Use when the user says "advisor", "second opinion", "what does X think", or wants an outside take without delegating the work itself.
- paseo-committee: Form a committee of two high-reasoning agents to step back, do root cause analysis, and produce a plan. Use when stuck, looping, tunnel-visioning, or facing a hard planning problem.
- paseo-handoff: Hand off the current task to another agent with full context. Use when the user says "handoff", "hand off", "hand this to", or wants to pass work to another agent.
- paseo-loop: Run an agent loop until an exit condition is met. Use when the user says "loop", "babysit", "keep trying until", "check every X", "watch", or wants iterative autonomous execution.
- skills: Reference codebase for Crates. Use this skill when you need to understand the structure, implementation patterns, or code details of the Crates project.
- zeroclaw: ZeroClaw Quick Reference
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# Design — netmaker-appliance-nested-blob
2	
3	## Goal
4	
5	Collapse the whole netmaker stack into **one self-contained Incus container**
6	(systemd-owned internally, no NIC, UDS/gRPC only), describe it as **one nested
7	plugin schema**, seal it as **one self-describing btrfs-image blob** that carries
8	both the control-plane `.blob`s and the bootable `/rootfs`, and **activate it by
9	loop-mounting** that image. Register = seal, deregister = remove.
10	
11	```
12	        ┌──────────────────────── HOST (Artix / s6) ────────────────────────┐
13	        │  s6d supervises the appliance as ONE unit (incus up/down)          │
14	        │                                                                    │
15	        │  op-grpc-bridge ──UDS──▶ durable socket in /rootfs/run/opdbus/     │
16	        │        ▲                        │                                  │
17	        │        │ reflection from        │ CallMethod{plugin_id, method}    │
18	        │        │ appliance blob         ▼                                  │
19	        │  ActiveReflectionCatalog   ┌───────────────────────────────────┐  │
20	        │  (tmpfs /dev/shm)          │  INCUS CONTAINER  (bare-metal-like)│  │
21	        │        ▲ loads /blobs      │  root = /rootfs subvolume (loop-ro)│  │
22	        │        │                   │  systemd owns (all from source):   │  │
23	        │  ┌─────┴───────────────┐   │    • netmaker (REST backend)       │  │
24	        │  │ appliance btrfs img │   │    • netclient  (OQ-1: wg iface)   │  │
25	        │  │  /blobs/<id>/*.blob │   │    • emqx  (MQTT, replaces mosq.)  │  │
26	        │  │  /rootfs (bootable, │   │    • rust-network-mgr (owns durable│  │
27	        │  │   incl. socket dir) │   │      socket + wg/nftables interior)│  │
28	        │  │  /blob-index.json   │   │  all inter-service comms LOCAL     │  │
29	        │  └─────────────────────┘   └───────────────────────────────────┘  │
30	        └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
31	```
32	
33	No NIC on the container; the only external surface is the UDS the bridge dials.
34	The socket is part of `/rootfs`, so it is present by construction on mount (no
35	proxy device, no bind-mount, no watcher). The WireGuard interface (if OQ-1(a))
36	is the identity fabric, not general I/O, and is managed inside by
37	`rust-network-mgr`.
38	
39	---
40	
41	## Nesting is native (was OQ-2 — resolved)
42	
43	There is no composite-vs-bundle fork. The appliance is **one composite plugin**
44	(`plugin_id = "netmaker_appliance"`) whose *state struct nests the child
45	capability structs* (`netmaker`, `netclient`, `emqx`, …). schemars emits their
46	`$defs`; `op-blob/src/adapter.rs` inlines them, `descriptor.rs` builds the
47	nested proto messages, both are sealed into the blob, and the `schema_renderer`
48	/ `json_render` plugins render them. Result: one `plugin_id`, one
49	`schema_hash16`, one D-Bus object, one `CallMethod` surface, no bespoke
50	aggregation layer. Method names are namespaced by child, e.g.
51	`netmaker.join_network`, `netclient.status`, `emqx.list_clients`.
52	
53	Subids use the existing plugin-scoped `op_blob::inject_common_subids` pattern.
54	The adapter intentionally ingests only top-level subids into the uniqueness map,
55	so nested-section fields do not collide; there is no "carry-up" work.
56	
57	### OQ-1 — WireGuard exception (still open)
58	
59	Design assumes **OQ-1(a)** unless the owner says otherwise: `netclient` brings
60	up the WG interface inside the container as the zero-trust identity fabric;
61	management and data still ride UDS/gRPC; the container has no *other* NIC. If
62	OQ-1(b) is chosen, an added task inserts a mesh-membership shim so the container
63	has zero kernel network interfaces (larger, deferred).
64	
65	---
66	
67	## Component 1 — Composite appliance plugin (`op-plugins`)
68	
69	No new aggregation builder. The appliance is an ordinary plugin whose state
70	struct nests the child capability structs; schemars + `op-blob`'s existing
71	`$defs` inlining and descriptor builder do the rest.
72	
73	```rust
74	// crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/appliance/netmaker_appliance.rs (new)
75	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema, Default)]
76	#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.software.plugin.netmaker-appliance.schema@v1"))]
77	pub struct NetmakerApplianceState {
78	    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.service.netmaker-appliance.netmaker@v1"))]
79	    pub netmaker: NetmakerState,      // child struct → emitted as a $def
80	    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.service.netmaker-appliance.netclient@v1"))]
81	    pub netclient: NetclientState,    // child struct → emitted as a $def
82	    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.service.netmaker-appliance.emqx@v1"))]
83	    pub emqx: EmqxState,              // child struct → emitted as a $def
84	}
85	```
86	
87	- schemars emits `$defs` for the nested structs; `adapter.rs` inlines them and
88	  `descriptor.rs` builds nested proto messages — sealed into the blob, rendered
89	  by the renderer (no carry-up code).
90	- Determinism (REQ-3.3) is the existing `op-blob` seal: canonical JSON, sorted,
91	  no timestamps → deterministic `schema_hash16`. Reused, not re-implemented.
92	- Subids: appliance-level subids on the fields above; shared nested-section
93	  subids via `op_blob::inject_common_subids` after schema build. New
94	  appliance-level subids are registered in `oscal_subid_registry.rs`.
95	
96	---
97	
98	## Component 2 — `/rootfs` extension of the btrfs image (`op-blob`)
99	
100	Extend `seal_blobs_into_btrfs_image` (or add a sibling
101	`seal_appliance_image`) so the staging tree gains a `rootfs/` directory that
102	`mkfs.btrfs --rootdir` populates as a subvolume alongside `blobs/`.
103	
104	```
105	staging/
106	  blobs/<child>/<child>.<hash16>.blob        (existing)
107	  blobs/netmaker_appliance/…blob             (composite identity blob)
108	  rootfs/                                     (NEW subvolume — bootable FS)
109	    usr/bin/{netmaker,netclient,emqx,rust-network-mgr}   (all from source)
110	    etc/systemd/system/*.service
111	    etc/emqx/…  etc/netclient/…
112	    run/opdbus/                               (durable gRPC socket dir — REQ-2.5)
113	  blob-index.json                             (extended: rootfs + appliance id)
114	```
115	
116	```rust
117	// op-blob/src/btrfs.rs (extended)
118	pub struct ApplianceImageReport {
119	    pub base: BtrfsImageReport,      // reuse existing fields
120	    pub has_rootfs: bool,
121	    pub appliance_id: String,
122	    pub rootfs_subvol: String,       // "rootfs"
123	}
124	```
125	
126	- Sealing stays `mkfs.btrfs --rootdir --shrink` (mountless, root-free) with an
127	  extra `--subvol rootfs`.
128	- `blob-index.json` gains:
129	  ```json
130	  {
131	    "format": "opdbus-blob-image/2",
132	    "appliance": { "plugin_id": "netmaker_appliance", "schema_hash": "…" },
133	    "rootfs": { "subvol": "rootfs" },
134	    "blobs": [ … ]
135	  }
136	  ```
137	- Determinism note (REQ-4.2): file contents/layout are controlled; `mkfs.btrfs`
138	  metadata (fs UUID) is not guaranteed reproducible — document and, if needed,
139	  pass a fixed UUID. Any residual non-determinism is recorded, not hidden.
140	
141	**Activation** (host, on register / boot):
142	
143	```
144	mount -o loop,ro <appliance>.img /mnt/opdbus-appliance
145	# 1. catalog: load /mnt/opdbus-appliance/blobs/* into ActiveReflectionCatalog
146	# 2. container: incus config the container root to the /rootfs subvolume
147	#    (btrfs subvol as Incus rootfs); systemd inside boots the stack
148	```
149	
150	Runtime plugin reads still come from tmpfs catalog (REQ-8.3 / NFR-2); `/rootfs`
151	is never copied into `/dev/shm`.
152	
153	Because the durable socket dir (`/run/opdbus/`) is *part of `/rootfs`*, step 2
154	delivers the socket automatically: mounting the subvolume as the container root
155	makes the socket present. There is no `proxy` device and no bind-mount device to
156	attach, so nothing can silently fail to "stick," and no watcher is needed to
157	re-assert it (REQ-2.5 / REQ-6.1).
158	
159	---
160	
161	## Component 2b — Durable socket + in-appliance network manager (`rust-network-mgr`)
162	
163	The "hit or miss whether the plugin sticks to the container" symptom is now
164	understood to have been **ownership + transport**, not the delivery device:
165	- root-owned `container.sock` intermittently blocked non-root/xray connections —
166	  fixed by non-root ownership (`shared_socket.rs::apply_socket_permissions`,
167	  `GHOSTBRIDGE_SOCKET_UID/GID/MODE`);
168	- the forkproxy/TCP hop reset — fixed by **xray using a native Unix socket**
169	  end-to-end (`server.rs`: createsocket, not a raw Incus proxy device).
170	
171	With those in place the host shared socket is durable on its own. The appliance
172	still ships its socket inside the rootfs blob, but for **self-containment and
173	determinism** (the appliance carries its own non-root socket, deps sealed once),
174	not as a flakiness workaround:
175	
176	- **The socket is an artifact of the rootfs blob**, not a device. It binds
177	  inside the container (systemd-owned `rust-network-mgr`, built from source,
178	  holds the `UnixListener` for its lifetime — the same durable-listener pattern
179	  the existing `unix_socket`/`shared_unix_socket` plugins use). Its path lives
180	  under `/run/opdbus/` inside `/rootfs`, so present-state = the mount.
181	- **`rust-network-mgr` is sealed inside the appliance blob** (REQ-2.6). Its real
182	  capability (rtnetlink → nftables) is legitimate *here* because the appliance
183	  interior has a real network: netclient's WireGuard interface + the netmaker
184	  mesh. It manages that interior data plane and owns the durable socket. Its
185	  dependency tree is resolved once, at seal.
186	- **Host invariant intact.** None of this puts IP/nftables on the host control
187	  plane; the host still sees only the one gRPC/UDS surface. `rust-network-mgr`'s
188	  own extras (its axum REST port, its stdio MCP binary, its text control socket)
189	  are **not** exposed — only the durable gRPC socket crosses the boundary.
190	
191	> This is why `rust-network-mgr` is the piece worth keeping: not its
192	> nftables/Docker code for the host, but a from-source, blob-sealable owner of a
193	> durable in-appliance socket + WG/nftables interior.
194	
195	---
196	
197	## Component 3 — Appliance plugin surface (`op-plugins`)
198	
199	**No nested containers.** netmaker, netclient, and EMQX are **built from source**
200	and run directly under systemd inside one bare-metal-like Incus container — not
201	docker images, not multiple containers. The legacy `incus-compose.yaml`
202	(`image: docker:gravitl/netmaker…`, `mq`, `netmaker-ui`, prometheus, grafana,
203	exporter) is stale and removed (REQ-7.1).
204	
205	**Internal interface = netmaker's native REST backend.** The GUI (`netmaker-ui`)
206	and the reverse proxy are dropped; netmaker already exposes a REST API
207	(`REST_BACKEND=on`, `API_PORT`) on the container loopback. The plugin drives
208	netmaker through that REST endpoint over loopback/UDS *inside* the container.
209	netclient is driven via its internal systemd unit; EMQX carries node/MQTT comms.
210	The **host-facing** control plane stays gRPC/`CallMethod` — no REST/MQTT leaks to
211	the host (REQ-2.1/2.2). Replace the host-oriented `netmaker.rs` internals
212	(REQ-7.2); never a host `netclient`.
213	
214	Authoritative Method → child → transport table:
215	
216	| Appliance method            | Child      | Effect (inside container)                       | subid category |
217	|---|---|---|---|
218	| `netmaker.join_network`     | netmaker   | REST backend network join                       | `mut`          |
219	| `netmaker.leave_network`    | netmaker   | REST backend leave                              | `mut`          |
220	| `netmaker.list_networks`    | netmaker   | REST backend read networks                      | `obs`          |
221	| `netclient.status`          | netclient  | wg/mesh status (OQ-1)                            | `obs`          |
222	| `netclient.restart`         | netclient  | restart internal systemd unit                   | `mut`          |
223	| `emqx.list_clients`         | emqx       | broker client list                              | `obs`          |
224	| `emqx.get_stats`            | emqx       | broker metrics                                  | `obs`          |
225	| `appliance.status`          | appliance  | aggregate health of all internal units          | `obs`          |
226	| `appliance.snapshot`        | appliance  | `btrfs send`-able image snapshot                | `mut`          |
227	
228	Method names, subids, and `required_capability` come from the composite schema
229	(single source of truth); the table restates them for review, it does not add
230	them independently.
231	
232	---
233	
234	## Component 4 — gRPC bridge / reflection (`op-grpc-bridge`)
235	
236	- The bridge advertises appliance services from the **appliance blob's
237	  descriptor set** loaded into `ActiveReflectionCatalog` (REQ-2.3), not a
238	  static list. Existing container-internal reflection recognition is the seam
239	  to extend.
240	- The current `grpc_client.rs::netmaker_*` direct-proto client
241	  (`netmaker_service_client::NetmakerServiceClient`, `netmaker_join`, …) is
242	  reviewed: if it bypasses `CallMethod`, it is retargeted through the plugin
243	  surface (REQ-2.2). No new `operation.<domain>.v1` package.
244	
245	---
246	
247	## File layout after this spec
248	
249	```
250	crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/
251	  appliance/mod.rs                  NEW — module wiring for the appliance plugin
252	  appliance/netmaker_appliance.rs   NEW — composite plugin: state nests child
253	                                          structs ($defs exported + rendered)
254	  netmaker.rs                       EDIT — drop host-netclient paths (REQ-7.2)
255	  oscal_subid_registry.rs           EDIT — appliance subids
256	
257	crates/op-blob/src/
258	  btrfs.rs                          EDIT — /rootfs subvolume + blob-index v2
259	  catalog.rs                        (unchanged; consumes /blobs as today)
260	
261	crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/
262	  grpc_client.rs                    EDIT — retarget netmaker_* via CallMethod
263	  (reflection wiring)               EDIT — advertise from appliance blob
264	
265	deploy/netmaker/
266	  appliance/                        NEW — from-source rootfs staging (netmaker,
267	                                          netclient, emqx, rust-network-mgr +
268	                                          systemd units, configs, run/opdbus/)
269	  incus-compose.yaml                REMOVE — stale docker/multi-container (REQ-7.1)
270	  mosquitto.conf, host-mosquitto.conf  REMOVE (EMQX replaces)
271	  rumqttd.toml                      REMOVE stale host-broker narrative (REQ-1.4)
272	```
273	
274	---
275	
276	## Determinism & durability
277	
278	- Appliance `schema_hash` is deterministic over the composite JSON (sorted, no
279	  timestamps) — the artifact identity in `<plugin_id>.<hash16>.blob`.
280	- Image byte-determinism is best-effort per REQ-4.2; the schema-blob layer is
281	  fully deterministic regardless of the rootfs.
282	- Durability = `op-blockchain` per-mutation chain + btrfs snapshot /
283	  `send`/`receive`. No SQL for state; no separate snapshot backups.
284	
285	## What is explicitly NOT changed
286	
287	- The tmpfs runtime catalog and `catalog_hash` computation (one-schema rule).
288	- The sealed `OPBLOB01` byte format and section layout.
289	- Host s6 supervision model; only the *container internals* use systemd.
290	- Frontend (lovable).

## Component 1 — Composite appliance plugin (`op-plugins`)

No new aggregation builder. The appliance is an ordinary plugin whose state
struct nests the child capability structs; schemars + `op-blob`'s existing
`$defs` inlining and descriptor builder do the rest.

```rust
// crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/appliance/netmaker_appliance.rs (new)
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema, Default)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.software.plugin.netmaker-appliance.schema@v1"))]
pub struct NetmakerApplianceState {
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.service.netmaker-appliance.netmaker@v1"))]
    pub netmaker: NetmakerState,      // child struct → emitted as a $def
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.service.netmaker-appliance.netclient@v1"))]
    pub netclient: NetclientState,    // child struct → emitted as a $def
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.service.netmaker-appliance.emqx@v1"))]
    pub emqx: EmqxState,              // child struct → emitted as a $def
}
```

- schemars emits `$defs` for the nested structs; `adapter.rs` inlines them and
  `descriptor.rs` builds nested proto messages — sealed into the blob, rendered
  by the renderer (no carry-up code).
- Determinism (REQ-3.3) is the existing `op-blob` seal: canonical JSON, sorted,
  no timestamps → deterministic `schema_hash16`. Reused, not re-implemented.
- Subids: appliance-level subids on the fields above; shared nested-section
  subids via `op_blob::inject_common_subids` after schema build. New
  appliance-level subids are registered in `oscal_subid_registry.rs`.

---

## Component 2 — `/rootfs` extension of the btrfs image (`op-blob`)

Extend `seal_blobs_into_btrfs_image` (or add a sibling
`seal_appliance_image`) so the staging tree gains a `rootfs/` directory that
`mkfs.btrfs --rootdir` populates as a subvolume alongside `blobs/`.

```
staging/
  blobs/<child>/<child>.<hash16>.blob        (existing)
  blobs/netmaker_appliance/…blob             (composite identity blob)
  rootfs/                                     (NEW subvolume — bootable FS)
    usr/bin/{netmaker,netclient,emqx,rust-network-mgr}   (all from source)
    etc/systemd/system/*.service
    etc/emqx/…  etc/netclient/…
    run/opdbus/                               (durable gRPC socket dir — REQ-2.5)
  blob-index.json                             (extended: rootfs + appliance id)
```

```rust
// op-blob/src/btrfs.rs (extended)
pub struct ApplianceImageReport {
    pub base: BtrfsImageReport,      // reuse existing fields
    pub has_rootfs: bool,
    pub appliance_id: String,
    pub rootfs_subvol: String,       // "rootfs"
}
```

- Sealing stays `mkfs.btrfs --rootdir --shrink` (mountless, root-free) with an
  extra `--subvol rootfs`.
- `blob-index.json` gains:
  ```json
  {
    "format": "opdbus-blob-image/2",
    "appliance": { "plugin_id": "netmaker_appliance", "schema_hash": "…" },
    "rootfs": { "subvol": "rootfs" },
    "blobs": [ … ]
  }
  ```
- Determinism note (REQ-4.2): file contents/layout are controlled; `mkfs.btrfs`
  metadata (fs UUID) is not guaranteed reproducible — document and, if needed,
  pass a fixed UUID. Any residual non-determinism is recorded, not hidden.

**Activation** (host, on register / boot):

```
mount -o loop,ro <appliance>.img /mnt/opdbus-appliance
# 1. catalog: load /mnt/opdbus-appliance/blobs/* into ActiveReflectionCatalog
# 2. container: incus config the container root to the /rootfs subvolume
#    (btrfs subvol as Incus rootfs); systemd inside boots the stack
```

Runtime plugin reads still come from tmpfs catalog (REQ-8.3 / NFR-2); `/rootfs`
is never copied into `/dev/shm`.

Because the durable socket dir (`/run/opdbus/`) is *part of `/rootfs`*, step 2
delivers the socket automatically: mounting the subvolume as the container root
makes the socket present. There is no `proxy` device and no bind-mount device to
attach, so nothing can silently fail to "stick," and no watcher is needed to
re-assert it (REQ-2.5 / REQ-6.1).

---

## Component 2b — Durable socket + in-appliance network manager (`rust-network-mgr`)

The "hit or miss whether the plugin sticks to the container" symptom is now
understood to have been **ownership + transport**, not the delivery device:
- root-owned `container.sock` intermittently blocked non-root/xray connections —
  fixed by non-root ownership (`shared_socket.rs::apply_socket_permissions`,
  `GHOSTBRIDGE_SOCKET_UID/GID/MODE`);
- the forkproxy/TCP hop reset — fixed by **xray using a native Unix socket**
  end-to-end (`server.rs`: createsocket, not a raw Incus proxy device).

With those in place the host shared socket is durable on its own. The appliance
still ships its socket inside the rootfs blob, but for **self-containment and
determinism** (the appliance carries its own non-root socket, deps sealed once),
not as a flakiness workaround:

- **The socket is an artifact of the rootfs blob**, not a device. It binds
  inside the container (systemd-owned `rust-network-mgr`, built from source,
  holds the `UnixListener` for its lifetime — the same durable-listener pattern
  the existing `unix_socket`/`shared_unix_socket` plugins use). Its path lives
  under `/run/opdbus/` inside `/rootfs`, so present-state = the mount.
- **`rust-network-mgr` is sealed inside the appliance blob** (REQ-2.6). Its real
  capability (rtnetlink → nftables) is legitimate *here* because the appliance
  interior has a real network: netclient's WireGuard interface + the netmaker
  mesh. It manages that interior data plane and owns the durable socket. Its
  dependency tree is resolved once, at seal.
- **Host invariant intact.** None of this puts IP/nftables on the host control
  plane; the host still sees only the one gRPC/UDS surface. `rust-network-mgr`'s
  own extras (its axum REST port, its stdio MCP binary, its text control socket)
  are **not** exposed — only the durable gRPC socket crosses the boundary.

> This is why `rust-network-mgr` is the piece worth keeping: not its
> nftables/Docker code for the host, but a from-source, blob-sealable owner of a
> durable in-appliance socket + WG/nftables interior.

---

## Component 3 — Appliance plugin surface (`op-plugins`)

**No nested containers.** netmaker, netclient, and EMQX are **built from source**
and run directly under systemd inside one bare-metal-like Incus container — not
docker images, not multiple containers. The legacy `incus-compose.yaml`
(`image: docker:gravitl/netmaker…`, `mq`, `netmaker-ui`, prometheus, grafana,
exporter) is stale and removed (REQ-7.1).

**Internal interface = netmaker's native REST backend.** The GUI (`netmaker-ui`)
and the reverse proxy are dropped; netmaker already exposes a REST API
(`REST_BACKEND=on`, `API_PORT`) on the container loopback. The plugin drives
netmaker through that REST endpoint over loopback/UDS *inside* the container.
netclient is driven via its internal systemd unit; EMQX carries node/MQTT comms.
The **host-facing** control plane stays gRPC/`CallMethod` — no REST/MQTT leaks to
the host (REQ-2.1/2.2). Replace the host-oriented `netmaker.rs` internals
(REQ-7.2); never a host `netclient`.

Authoritative Method → child → transport table:

| Appliance method            | Child      | Effect (inside container)                       | subid category |
|---|---|---|---|
| `netmaker.join_network`     | netmaker   | REST backend network join                       | `mut`          |
| `netmaker.leave_network`    | netmaker   | REST backend leave                              | `mut`          |
| `netmaker.list_networks`    | netmaker   | REST backend read networks                      | `obs`          |
| `netclient.status`          | netclient  | wg/mesh status (OQ-1)                            | `obs`          |
| `netclient.restart`         | netclient  | restart internal systemd unit                   | `mut`          |
| `emqx.list_clients`         | emqx       | broker client list                              | `obs`          |
| `emqx.get_stats`            | emqx       | broker metrics                                  | `obs`          |
| `appliance.status`          | appliance  | aggregate health of all internal units          | `obs`          |
| `appliance.snapshot`        | appliance  | `btrfs send`-able image snapshot                | `mut`          |

Method names, subids, and `required_capability` come from the composite schema
(single source of truth); the table restates them for review, it does not add
them independently.

---

## Component 4 — gRPC bridge / reflection (`op-grpc-bridge`)

- The bridge advertises appliance services from the **appliance blob's
  descriptor set** loaded into `ActiveReflectionCatalog` (REQ-2.3), not a
  static list. Existing container-internal reflection recognition is the seam
  to extend.
- The current `grpc_client.rs::netmaker_*` direct-proto client
  (`netmaker_service_client::NetmakerServiceClient`, `netmaker_join`, …) is
  reviewed: if it bypasses `CallMethod`, it is retargeted through the plugin
  surface (REQ-2.2). No new `operation.<domain>.v1` package.

---

## File layout after this spec

```
crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/
  appliance/mod.rs                  NEW — module wiring for the appliance plugin
  appliance/netmaker_appliance.rs   NEW — composite plugin: state nests child
                                          structs ($defs exported + rendered)
  netmaker.rs                       EDIT — drop host-netclient paths (REQ-7.2)
  oscal_subid_registry.rs           EDIT — appliance subids

crates/op-blob/src/
  btrfs.rs                          EDIT — /rootfs subvolume + blob-index v2
  catalog.rs                        (unchanged; consumes /blobs as today)

crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/
  grpc_client.rs                    EDIT — retarget netmaker_* via CallMethod
  (reflection wiring)               EDIT — advertise from appliance blob

deploy/netmaker/
  appliance/                        NEW — from-source rootfs staging (netmaker,
                                          netclient, emqx, rust-network-mgr +
                                          systemd units, configs, run/opdbus/)
  incus-compose.yaml                REMOVE — stale docker/multi-container (REQ-7.1)
  mosquitto.conf, host-mosquitto.conf  REMOVE (EMQX replaces)
  rumqttd.toml                      REMOVE stale host-broker narrative (REQ-1.4)
```

---

## Determinism & durability

- Appliance `schema_hash` is deterministic over the composite JSON (sorted, no
  timestamps) — the artifact identity in `<plugin_id>.<hash16>.blob`.
- Image byte-determinism is best-effort per REQ-4.2; the schema-blob layer is
  fully deterministic regardless of the rootfs.
- Durability = `op-blockchain` per-mutation chain + btrfs snapshot /
  `send`/`receive`. No SQL for state; no separate snapshot backups.

## What is explicitly NOT changed

- The tmpfs runtime catalog and `catalog_hash` computation (one-schema rule).
- The sealed `OPBLOB01` byte format and section layout.
- Host s6 supervision model; only the *container internals* use systemd.
- Frontend (lovable).

## Phase 3 — Appliance plugin + bridge wiring

### Task 3.1 — `netmaker_appliance` composite plugin
**Requirements**: REQ-1.1, REQ-2.2, REQ-3.1, REQ-6.1
**Steps**:
1. Add `appliance/netmaker_appliance.rs` nesting `netmaker`, `netclient`,
   `emqx` via Task 1.1; register it in `default_registry.rs`.
2. Dispatch namespaced methods to netmaker's **REST backend** inside the
   container (GUI/reverse-proxy dropped) over the durable socket; host-facing
   stays gRPC/`CallMethod`. No polling/watchers.
**Gate**: `cargo check -p op-plugins` green; appliance appears in `ListPlugins`.

### Task 3.2 — Retarget `netmaker.rs` off host-`netclient`
**Requirements**: REQ-1.3, REQ-7.2
**Steps**:
1. Remove/redefine host-`netclient` fields and code paths
   (`installed`/`daemon_running`-under-s6/host `control_socket`,
   `check_netclient_installed`, host config read/write, host `restart_netclient`).
2. Point capability at the container-internal, systemd-owned service.
**Gate**: `cargo check -p op-plugins` green; no host `Command::new` for
`netclient` remains (grep clean).

### Task 3.3 — Bridge reflection from the appliance blob
**Requirements**: REQ-2.1, REQ-2.3
**Steps**:
1. In `op-grpc-bridge`, advertise appliance services from the appliance blob's
   descriptor set (not a static list); reuse existing container-internal
   reflection recognition.
2. Review `grpc_client.rs::netmaker_*`; if it bypasses `CallMethod`, retarget it
   through the plugin surface (no new proto package).
**Gate**: `cargo check -p op-grpc-bridge` green.

---

## Phase 4 — From-source single-container deploy + cleanup

### Task 4.1 — From-source appliance rootfs staging
**Requirements**: REQ-1.1, REQ-1.2, REQ-1.4, REQ-2.5, REQ-2.6
**Steps**:
1. Add `deploy/netmaker/appliance/` producing the `rootfs/` staging with the
   **from-source** binaries `netmaker` + `netclient` + `emqx` +
   `rust-network-mgr`, their `systemd` units, and EMQX + netclient configs.
   No docker, no nested containers, no `netmaker-ui`, no reverse proxy.
   Bootstrap scripts only (the blessed exception).
2. Include the durable socket dir `run/opdbus/` in the staging so the socket is
   part of `/rootfs` (REQ-2.5); a systemd unit runs `rust-network-mgr` which
   binds and holds it with **non-root ownership** and **native UDS** (the proven
   durability properties). No Incus proxy device, no bind-mount.
3. Wire the staging into `seal_appliance_image` (Task 2.1).
**Gate**: image builds; `verify_btrfs_image` true; `blob-index.json` v2 valid;
`/rootfs/run/opdbus` present in the sealed image.

### Task 4.2 — Remove stale multi-container / host-broker artifacts
**Requirements**: REQ-1.4, REQ-7.1
**Steps**:
1. Remove/replace `incus-compose.yaml`, `compose.yaml`, `mosquitto.conf`,
   `host-mosquitto.conf`; delete the stale host-broker `rumqttd.toml` narrative.
2. Grep the repo for "host broker" / host-`netclient` docs and reconcile.
**Gate**: `grep -rn "replaces the no-NIC" deploy/` empty; no doc describes a
host broker or host `netclient`.

---

## Phase 5 — (conditional) OQ-1(b) zero-NIC mesh shim
Only if the owner chose OQ-1(b) in Task 0.1. Adds a brokered mesh-membership
path so the container has zero kernel network interfaces. Deferred by default.

---

## Phase 6 — Final audit
**Requirements**: REQ-2.2, REQ-3.3, REQ-5.3, NFR-1
**Steps**:
1. `grep -rn "operation\..*\.v1" crates/` — no new appliance service package.
2. Confirm appliance `schema_hash` is stable across two builds (determinism).
3. Confirm the blob sealer in `op-blob` is the only writer of catalog blobs
   (SchemaEngine only reports the hash).
4. Confirm the durable socket ships inside `/rootfs` (no `proxy` device, no
   bind-mount, no watcher): grep the deploy + plugin code for `type: proxy` /
   bind-mount of the socket and for any watch/poll loop — all empty.
5. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and
   `cargo fmt --all -- --check` green.
**Gate**: all above green; OQ-1 recorded as resolved (OQ-2 already resolved).

52	## Ground Truth (verified 2026-07-06)
53	
54	**Already present (do not rebuild):**
55	
56	- `op-blob/src/btrfs.rs::seal_blobs_into_btrfs_image` seals a set of sealed
57	  `.blob` files into a btrfs image via `mkfs.btrfs --rootdir --shrink`
58	  (no mount, no root), one subvolume per plugin, writes `/blob-index.json`,
59	  verifies the superblock magic, and returns a `mount -o loop,ro` hint. The
60	  file's own docstring states the goal: a "complete deployment unit …
61	  mountable (loop/ro), snapshottable, `btrfs send/receive`-able, and
62	  self-describing."
63	- `op-blob/src/catalog.rs`: per-object shm layout
64	  `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob`;
65	  `catalog_hash` is a blake3 leaf-fold computed in exactly one place; consumers
66	  never re-hash. Runtime consumption stays on tmpfs (REQ-8.3: "never
67	  Btrfs-backed I/O") — the btrfs image is the at-rest/transport form.
68	- `op-blob/src/blob.rs`: deterministic sealed byte format `OPBLOB01` with
69	  sections (1 canonical `PluginSchema` JSON, 2 `BlobManifest`, 3
70	  `FileDescriptorSet`, 4 meta); `BlobManifest` couples schema/D-Bus/gRPC/
71	  descriptor identity and carries per-method `subid`, `required_capability`,
72	  `side_effect`, `idempotent`.
73	- **Nesting is native and already end-to-end.** `op-blob/src/adapter.rs`
74	  resolves `$defs`/`definitions` inline so nested structs expand;
75	  `op-blob/src/descriptor.rs` builds nested proto messages from the same defs.
76	  Both are sealed into the blob (schema-JSON section 1 + descriptor-set section
77	  3), and the `schema_renderer` / `json_render` plugins render them. So a
78	  composite appliance state struct that *nests* the child capability structs
79	  exports its `$defs` into the blob and is rendered by the renderer with no new
80	  aggregation machinery. There is **no** "subid carry-up gap": the adapter
81	  intentionally ingests only top-level subids into the uniqueness map, and
82	  nested-section subids follow the existing plugin-scoped
83	  `op_blob::inject_common_subids` pattern (a fixed subid baked into a shared
84	  nested struct would collide globally).
85	
86	**The real gap:**
87	
88	- The btrfs image holds only `.blob` control-plane artifacts today; it has **no
89	  `/rootfs`** subvolume for a bootable container filesystem.
90	- `netmaker.rs` assumes a **host** `netclient` under s6; it has no notion of a
91	  container-internal, systemd-owned stack driven over UDS/gRPC.
92	
93	---
94	
95	## Functional Requirements
96	
97	### REQ-1 — One Self-Contained Appliance Container
98	
99	**REQ-1.1** The netmaker stack MUST be one bare-metal-like Incus container
100	holding `netmaker`, `netclient`, and EMQX (and supporting services), all **built
101	from source** — no docker images, no nested containers. The legacy
102	`incus-compose.yaml` (docker-image, multi-container) is stale and MUST be
103	removed, not "converted." The web GUI (`netmaker-ui`) and reverse proxy are
104	dropped; netmaker's native REST backend is the only internal interface.
105	
106	**REQ-1.2** `systemd` inside the container owns the internal services. No
107	internal service may depend on the host init. The host control plane remains
108	s6; `s6d` supervises the container as one opaque unit (up/down via Incus).
109	
110	**REQ-1.3** `netclient` MUST run **inside** the container. No host-installed
111	`netclient` may be required. The `netmaker.rs` fields that assume a host
112	`netclient` (`installed`, `daemon_running` under s6, host `control_socket`
113	path) MUST be re-defined against the container-internal, systemd-owned service.
114	
115	**REQ-1.4** EMQX replaces Mosquitto as the MQTT broker **software only**. The
116	no-NIC + UDS transport model is unchanged. The stale `rumqttd.toml`
117	"host broker replaces the no-NIC container" narrative MUST be removed; there is
118	no host broker and no host `netclient` in this design.
119	
120	### REQ-2 — gRPC-Only, No NIC, UDS Transport
121	
122	**REQ-2.1** All host ↔ container I/O (management and data) MUST ride gRPC over
123	Unix domain sockets. The container MUST have no NIC and no IP for general I/O.
124	
125	**REQ-2.2** No new `operation.<domain>.v1` proto service package may be created
126	for the appliance. The appliance is a **plugin** registered via
127	`crates/op-plugins/src/default_registry.rs`; its surface is reached through
128	`PluginService.CallMethod`.
129	
130	**REQ-2.3** Container-internal service discovery MUST come from the appliance
131	blob's reflection descriptors / `blob-index.json`, never a hardcoded service
132	list. The gRPC bridge advertises only what the active appliance blob declares.
133	
134	**REQ-2.4 — Open Question (OQ-1, WireGuard exception).** `netclient` establishes
135	a WireGuard interface to join the mesh, but the invariant is "no NIC / all I/O
136	is UDS," and the WireGuard pubkey is also the identity layer. The spec MUST
137	record which of the following is intended, because it decides whether
138	`netclient`-in-container is straightforward or needs a shim:
139	- **(a)** the WG interface is the allowed exception (it is the zero-trust
140	  identity fabric, not general I/O); `netclient` brings it up internally and
141	  management/data still ride UDS+gRPC; **or**
142	- **(b)** even mesh membership is brokered so the container has zero kernel
143	  network interfaces.
144	This requirement is **not resolved by this spec**; it is flagged for the owner.
145	
146	**REQ-2.5 — Durable socket in the rootfs blob (no proxy, no bind-mount).** The
147	one gRPC control socket MUST reach the container by living inside the
148	loop-mounted rootfs blob, so it is present **by construction** whenever the
149	appliance is mounted. It MUST NOT be delivered via an Incus `proxy` device
150	(forkproxy) or an out-of-band directory bind-mount, and its presence MUST NOT
151	depend on any watcher, poll, or repair loop. Mounting the blob is the
152	present-state; unmounting removes it. The socket MUST keep the proven-durable
153	properties of the host shared socket: **non-root ownership**
154	(`shared_socket.rs::apply_socket_permissions`) and **native Unix-socket
155	transport** (xray native UDS, not a proxy/TCP hop) — these, not the blob, were
156	what fixed the earlier "hit or miss" flakiness; the blob adds self-containment
157	and determinism.
158	
159	**REQ-2.6 — In-appliance network manager, sealed once.** A network manager built
160	from source (`rust-network-mgr`) MUST be sealed **inside the appliance blob** to
161	own the durable socket and the container-internal WireGuard/nftables data plane
162	(the real network exists only *inside* the appliance; the host control plane
163	stays IP-free). Its dependency tree MUST be resolved at seal time only — no
164	per-host dependency resolution at activation. This capability is scoped to the
165	appliance interior; it MUST NOT introduce IP/nftables logic on the host control
166	plane.
167	
168	### REQ-3 — Nested / Composite Appliance Schema
169	
170	**REQ-3.1** The appliance MUST be one addressable D-Bus object
171	(`/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<appliance>`), i.e. one `plugin_id`, one deterministic
172	`schema_hash16`, one blob in the catalog.
173	
174	**REQ-3.2** The appliance state struct MUST nest the child capability structs
175	(`netmaker`, `netclient`, `emqx`, and any supporting service). schemars emits
176	their `$defs`; `op-blob/src/adapter.rs` inlines them and `descriptor.rs` builds
177	the nested proto messages, so the child shapes are exported into the blob and
178	rendered by the `schema_renderer` / `json_render` plugins — the native path, no
179	bespoke aggregation. Subids follow the existing plugin-scoped injection
180	(`op_blob::inject_common_subids`); nested-section fields deliberately stay out
181	of the top-level uniqueness map (a shared nested struct's fixed subid would
182	collide globally).
183	
184	**REQ-3.3** The composite `schema_hash` MUST be deterministic (one-schema rule):
185	the same nested state struct produces the same appliance `schema_hash` via the
186	existing `op-blob` seal (sorted, no timestamps). No separate aggregation step.
187	
188	**REQ-3.4** `mut.*` methods on child capabilities MUST retain `actor_id` +
189	`capability_id`; `evt.*` MUST retain `event_id`/`event_hash` through nesting.
190	Every new subid introduced by the appliance is registered in
191	`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/oscal_subid_registry.rs` (CI-enforced
192	uniqueness).
193	
194	**REQ-3.5 — Resolved (composite via native nesting).** The appliance is one
195	composite plugin whose state struct nests the child structs; `$defs` are
196	exported into the blob and rendered by the renderer (per Ground Truth). This is
197	**not** an open question — there is no separate "aggregate bundle" path to weigh,
198	because native `$defs` nesting already yields one plugin_id / one blob / one
199	rendered surface.
200	
201	### REQ-4 — Appliance Blob With `/rootfs` Subvolume
202	
203	**REQ-4.1** The at-rest appliance artifact MUST be a single btrfs image produced
204	through the existing `seal_blobs_into_btrfs_image` path (extended), containing:
205	- `/blobs/<plugin_id>/…` — the sealed schema/descriptor control-plane blobs
206	  (as today), and
207	- **`/rootfs`** — a subvolume holding the bootable container filesystem:
208	  the from-source `netmaker` + `netclient` + EMQX + `rust-network-mgr`
209	  binaries, systemd units, configs, **and the durable gRPC socket's directory**
210	  (REQ-2.5), so the socket is present by construction on mount.
211	
212	**REQ-4.2** Sealing MUST stay mountless and root-free where the existing path is
213	(`mkfs.btrfs --rootdir --shrink`). Determinism MUST be preserved: the same
214	rootfs staging + same blobs produce byte-identical images (sorted, no
215	timestamps) as far as `mkfs.btrfs` allows; any unavoidable non-determinism MUST
216	be documented.
217	
218	**REQ-4.3** Activation ("mount the blob") MUST loop-mount the image read-only,
219	load the reflection catalog from `/blobs`, and present `/rootfs` as the Incus
220	container root. Runtime plugin consumption stays on tmpfs (REQ-8.3); the btrfs
221	image is the at-rest/transport form.
222	
223	**REQ-4.4** The image MUST remain self-describing, snapshottable, and
224	`btrfs send/receive`-able (the btrfs.rs stated goal). `/blob-index.json` MUST be
225	extended to record the `/rootfs` subvolume and the appliance identity.
226	
227	### REQ-5 — Lifecycle: Register = Seal, Deregister = Remove
228	
229	**REQ-5.1** Registering the appliance MUST seal it (schema + rootfs) into the
230	image and place its control-plane blob(s) in the catalog. The appliance exists
231	⟺ its blob is in the catalog.
232	
233	**REQ-5.2** Deregistering MUST remove the blob(s) from the catalog and stop the
234	container as one unit. No orphaned host services, no lingering NIC.
235	
236	**REQ-5.3** The sole writer of catalog blobs remains the blob sealer in
237	`op-blob`. SchemaEngine (`op-projection`) only reports the published catalog
238	hash — it never writes appliance blobs.
239	
240	### REQ-6 — Reactive, Durable, No Polling
241	
242	**REQ-6.1** No polling loops, D-Bus watchers, indexing, or caching in appliance
243	plugin/service code. State transitions are reactive (arrival-triggered /
244	mutation-triggered). The durable socket (REQ-2.5) sticks **structurally** (it is
245	part of the mounted blob), never via a watch/repair loop.
246	
247	**REQ-6.2** Durability is the per-mutation immutable chain (`op-blockchain`).
248	No SQL for state; no snapshot backups of appliance state beyond the blob's own
249	snapshot/`send`-`receive` capability.
250	
251	### REQ-7 — Deprecations / Cleanup
252	
253	**REQ-7.1** `deploy/netmaker/incus-compose.yaml`, `compose.yaml`,
254	`mosquitto.conf`, `host-mosquitto.conf`, and the stale `rumqttd.toml` narrative
255	MUST be reconciled with the single-container design (removed or rewritten). No
256	document may keep describing a host broker or a host `netclient`.
257	
258	**REQ-7.2** `netmaker.rs` host-`netclient` code paths MUST be removed or
259	retargeted to the container-internal, UDS/gRPC-driven service per REQ-1.3.
260	
261	---
262	
263	## Non-Functional Requirements
264	
265	**NFR-1 (build/gates).** `cargo check -p op-blob`, `-p op-plugins`,
266	`-p op-grpc-bridge` MUST be green after each phase; `cargo clippy --workspace
267	--all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
268	green at the end.
269	
270	**NFR-2 (size/RAM).** A bootable `/rootfs` is far larger than a schema blob. It
271	MUST live only in the loop-mounted btrfs image, never in `/dev/shm`. The tmpfs
272	catalog materializes only schema/descriptor bytes.
273	
274	**NFR-3 (Rust-first).** No new Python. `anyhow`/`thiserror`, `simd_json`
275	preferred. No `Command::new` in plugin/service code except the already-blessed
276	`mkfs.btrfs` sealing path and bootstrap scripts.
277	
278	**NFR-4 (subids).** Every new method/surface carries a subid per the taxonomy
279	and is registered in `oscal_subid_registry.rs`.
280	
281	---
282	
283	## Out of Scope
284	
285	- Frontend / UI work (handled separately by lovable).
286	- The btrfs *inside* ordinary plugin blobs treated as unmounted subvolumes —
287	  that is the btrfs control-panel view, explicitly the lowest priority and not
288	  part of this appliance work.
289	- Resolving OQ-1 (WireGuard exception) — recorded for the owner; design.md gives
290	  a recommendation only. (OQ-2 is resolved: composite via native `$defs`
291	  nesting, REQ-3.5.)
292

  resolves `$defs`/`definitions` inline so nested structs expand;
  `op-blob/src/descriptor.rs` builds nested proto messages from the same defs.
  Both are sealed into the blob (schema-JSON section 1 + descriptor-set section
  3), and the `schema_renderer` / `json_render` plugins render them. So a
  composite appliance state struct that *nests* the child capability structs
  exports its `$defs` into the blob and is rendered by the renderer with no new
  aggregation machinery. There is **no** "subid carry-up gap": the adapter
  intentionally ingests only top-level subids into the uniqueness map, and
  nested-section subids follow the existing plugin-scoped
  `op_blob::inject_common_subids` pattern (a fixed subid baked into a shared
  nested struct would collide globally).

**The real gap:**

- The btrfs image holds only `.blob` control-plane artifacts today; it has **no
  `/rootfs`** subvolume for a bootable container filesystem.
- `netmaker.rs` assumes a **host** `netclient` under s6; it has no notion of a
  container-internal, systemd-owned stack driven over UDS/gRPC.

---

## Functional Requirements

### REQ-1 — One Self-Contained Appliance Container

**REQ-1.1** The netmaker stack MUST be one bare-metal-like Incus container
holding `netmaker`, `netclient`, and EMQX (and supporting services), all **built
from source** — no docker images, no nested containers. The legacy
`incus-compose.yaml` (docker-image, multi-container) is stale and MUST be
removed, not "converted." The web GUI (`netmaker-ui`) and reverse proxy are
dropped; netmaker's native REST backend is the only internal interface.

**REQ-1.2** `systemd` inside the container owns the internal services. No
internal service may depend on the host init. The host control plane remains
s6; `s6d` supervises the container as one opaque unit (up/down via Incus).

**REQ-1.3** `netclient` MUST run **inside** the container. No host-installed
`netclient` may be required. The `netmaker.rs` fields that assume a host
`netclient` (`installed`, `daemon_running` under s6, host `control_socket`
path) MUST be re-defined against the container-internal, systemd-owned service.

**REQ-1.4** EMQX replaces Mosquitto as the MQTT broker **software only**. The
no-NIC + UDS transport model is unchanged. The stale `rumqttd.toml`
"host broker replaces the no-NIC container" narrative MUST be removed; there is
no host broker and no host `netclient` in this design.

### REQ-2 — gRPC-Only, No NIC, UDS Transport

**REQ-2.1** All host ↔ container I/O (management and data) MUST ride gRPC over
Unix domain sockets. The container MUST have no NIC and no IP for general I/O.

**REQ-2.2** No new `operation.<domain>.v1` proto service package may be created
for the appliance. The appliance is a **plugin** registered via
`crates/op-plugins/src/default_registry.rs`; its surface is reached through
`PluginService.CallMethod`.

**REQ-2.3** Container-internal service discovery MUST come from the appliance
blob's reflection descriptors / `blob-index.json`, never a hardcoded service
list. The gRPC bridge advertises only what the active appliance blob declares.

**REQ-2.4 — Open Question (OQ-1, WireGuard exception).** `netclient` establishes
a WireGuard interface to join the mesh, but the invariant is "no NIC / all I/O
is UDS," and the WireGuard pubkey is also the identity layer. The spec MUST
record which of the following is intended, because it decides whether
`netclient`-in-container is straightforward or needs a shim:
- **(a)** the WG interface is the allowed exception (it is the zero-trust
  identity fabric, not general I/O); `netclient` brings it up internally and
  management/data still ride UDS+gRPC; **or**
- **(b)** even mesh membership is brokered so the container has zero kernel
  network interfaces.
This requirement is **not resolved by this spec**; it is flagged for the owner.

**REQ-2.5 — Durable socket in the rootfs blob (no proxy, no bind-mount).** The
one gRPC control socket MUST reach the container by living inside the
loop-mounted rootfs blob, so it is present **by construction** whenever the
appliance is mounted. It MUST NOT be delivered via an Incus `proxy` device
(forkproxy) or an out-of-band directory bind-mount, and its presence MUST NOT
depend on any watcher, poll, or repair loop. Mounting the blob is the
present-state; unmounting removes it. The socket MUST keep the proven-durable
properties of the host shared socket: **non-root ownership**
(`shared_socket.rs::apply_socket_permissions`) and **native Unix-socket
transport** (xray native UDS, not a proxy/TCP hop) — these, not the blob, were
what fixed the earlier "hit or miss" flakiness; the blob adds self-containment
and determinism.

**REQ-2.6 — In-appliance network manager, sealed once.** A network manager built
from source (`rust-network-mgr`) MUST be sealed **inside the appliance blob** to
own the durable socket and the container-internal WireGuard/nftables data plane
(the real network exists only *inside* the appliance; the host control plane
stays IP-free). Its dependency tree MUST be resolved at seal time only — no
per-host dependency resolution at activation. This capability is scoped to the
appliance interior; it MUST NOT introduce IP/nftables logic on the host control
plane.

### REQ-3 — Nested / Composite Appliance Schema

**REQ-3.1** The appliance MUST be one addressable D-Bus object
(`/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<appliance>`), i.e. one `plugin_id`, one deterministic
`schema_hash16`, one blob in the catalog.

**REQ-3.2** The appliance state struct MUST nest the child capability structs
(`netmaker`, `netclient`, `emqx`, and any supporting service). schemars emits
their `$defs`; `op-blob/src/adapter.rs` inlines them and `descriptor.rs` builds
the nested proto messages, so the child shapes are exported into the blob and
rendered by the `schema_renderer` / `json_render` plugins — the native path, no
bespoke aggregation. Subids follow the existing plugin-scoped injection
(`op_blob::inject_common_subids`); nested-section fields deliberately stay out
of the top-level uniqueness map (a shared nested struct's fixed subid would
collide globally).

**REQ-3.3** The composite `schema_hash` MUST be deterministic (one-schema rule):
the same nested state struct produces the same appliance `schema_hash` via the
existing `op-blob` seal (sorted, no timestamps). No separate aggregation step.

**REQ-3.4** `mut.*` methods on child capabilities MUST retain `actor_id` +
`capability_id`; `evt.*` MUST retain `event_id`/`event_hash` through nesting.
Every new subid introduced by the appliance is registered in
`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/oscal_subid_registry.rs` (CI-enforced
uniqueness).

**REQ-3.5 — Resolved (composite via native nesting).** The appliance is one
composite plugin whose state struct nests the child structs; `$defs` are
exported into the blob and rendered by the renderer (per Ground Truth). This is
**not** an open question — there is no separate "aggregate bundle" path to weigh,
because native `$defs` nesting already yields one plugin_id / one blob / one
rendered surface.

### REQ-4 — Appliance Blob With `/rootfs` Subvolume

**REQ-4.1** The at-rest appliance artifact MUST be a single btrfs image produced
through the existing `seal_blobs_into_btrfs_image` path (extended), containing:
- `/blobs/<plugin_id>/…` — the sealed schema/descriptor control-plane blobs
  (as today), and
- **`/rootfs`** — a subvolume holding the bootable container filesystem:
  the from-source `netmaker` + `netclient` + EMQX + `rust-network-mgr`
  binaries, systemd units, configs, **and the durable gRPC socket's directory**
  (REQ-2.5), so the socket is present by construction on mount.

**REQ-4.2** Sealing MUST stay mountless and root-free where the existing path is
(`mkfs.btrfs --rootdir --shrink`). Determinism MUST be preserved: the same
rootfs staging + same blobs produce byte-identical images (sorted, no
timestamps) as far as `mkfs.btrfs` allows; any unavoidable non-determinism MUST
be documented.

**REQ-4.3** Activation ("mount the blob") MUST loop-mount the image read-only,
load the reflection catalog from `/blobs`, and present `/rootfs` as the Incus
container root. Runtime plugin consumption stays on tmpfs (REQ-8.3); the btrfs
image is the at-rest/transport form.

**REQ-4.4** The image MUST remain self-describing, snapshottable, and
`btrfs send/receive`-able (the btrfs.rs stated goal). `/blob-index.json` MUST be
extended to record the `/rootfs` subvolume and the appliance identity.

### REQ-5 — Lifecycle: Register = Seal, Deregister = Remove

**REQ-5.1** Registering the appliance MUST seal it (schema + rootfs) into the
image and place its control-plane blob(s) in the catalog. The appliance exists
⟺ its blob is in the catalog.

**REQ-5.2** Deregistering MUST remove the blob(s) from the catalog and stop the
container as one unit. No orphaned host services, no lingering NIC.

**REQ-5.3** The sole writer of catalog blobs remains the blob sealer in
`op-blob`. SchemaEngine (`op-projection`) only reports the published catalog
hash — it never writes appliance blobs.

### REQ-6 — Reactive, Durable, No Polling

**REQ-6.1** No polling loops, D-Bus watchers, indexing, or caching in appliance
plugin/service code. State transitions are reactive (arrival-triggered /
mutation-triggered). The durable socket (REQ-2.5) sticks **structurally** (it is
part of the mounted blob), never via a watch/repair loop.

**REQ-6.2** Durability is the per-mutation immutable chain (`op-blockchain`).
No SQL for state; no snapshot backups of appliance state beyond the blob's own
snapshot/`send`-`receive` capability.

### REQ-7 — Deprecations / Cleanup

**REQ-7.1** `deploy/netmaker/incus-compose.yaml`, `compose.yaml`,
`mosquitto.conf`, `host-mosquitto.conf`, and the stale `rumqttd.toml` narrative
MUST be reconciled with the single-container design (removed or rewritten). No
document may keep describing a host broker or a host `netclient`.

**REQ-7.2** `netmaker.rs` host-`netclient` code paths MUST be removed or
retargeted to the container-internal, UDS/gRPC-driven service per REQ-1.3.

---

## Non-Functional Requirements

**NFR-1 (build/gates).** `cargo check -p op-blob`, `-p op-plugins`,
`-p op-grpc-bridge` MUST be green after each phase; `cargo clippy --workspace
--all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
green at the end.

**NFR-2 (size/RAM).** A bootable `/rootfs` is far larger than a schema blob. It
MUST live only in the loop-mounted btrfs image, never in `/dev/shm`. The tmpfs
catalog materializes only schema/descriptor bytes.

**NFR-3 (Rust-first).** No new Python. `anyhow`/`thiserror`, `simd_json`
preferred. No `Command::new` in plugin/service code except the already-blessed
`mkfs.btrfs` sealing path and bootstrap scripts.

**NFR-4 (subids).** Every new method/surface carries a subid per the taxonomy
and is registered in `oscal_subid_registry.rs`.

---

## Out of Scope

- Frontend / UI work (handled separately by lovable).
- The btrfs *inside* ordinary plugin blobs treated as unmounted subvolumes —
  that is the btrfs control-panel view, explicitly the lowest priority and not
  part of this appliance work.
- Resolving OQ-1 (WireGuard exception) — recorded for the owner; design.md gives
  a recommendation only. (OQ-2 is resolved: composite via native `$defs`
  nesting, REQ-3.5.)

=== deploy/s6/wg-netmaker/run ===
#!/bin/sh
# wg-netmaker - Netmaker WireGuard mesh network service
# AGENTS.md: D-Bus-first, gbr_* naming for privacy network

# Load Netmaker configuration
NETMAKER_SERVER="${NETMAKER_SERVER:-netmaker.3tched.com}"
NETMAKER_NETWORK="${NETMAKER_NETWORK:-ghostbridge}"

# Check for netclient binary
if [ -x /usr/local/bin/netclient ]; then
    exec 2>&1
    exec /usr/local/bin/netclient daemon
elif [ -x /usr/bin/netclient ]; then
    exec 2>&1
    exec /usr/bin/netclient daemon
else
    echo "Error: netclient binary not found"
    exit 1
fi

=== deploy/s6/netmaker-rumqttd/run ===
#!/bin/sh
# Unit name "netmaker-rumqttd" is historical (matches the installed live
# service in /etc/s6/sv); the broker is now mosquitto — netmaker only
# requires MQTT, the broker impl is swappable.
set -eu
exec 2>&1

exec /usr/bin/mosquitto -c /home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto/deploy/netmaker/host-mosquitto.conf

=== deploy/s6/op-grpc-bridge-zeroclaw/run ===
#!/bin/sh
# 🟢 🛷 Zeroclaw Axum Host — gRPC / gRPC-Web schema bridge
#
# Serves the zeroclaw schema from its sealed blob in /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs.
# Depends on opblob having sealed the plugin catalog first.

set -eu
exec 2>&1

if [ -r /etc/op-dbus/environment ]; then
  set -a
  . /etc/op-dbus/environment
  set +a
fi

export DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS
: "${DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS:?DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS must be set in /etc/op-dbus/environment}"
export ZEROCLAW_BIND_ADDR="${ZEROCLAW_BIND_ADDR:-0.0.0.0:8090}"
export ZEROCLAW_SCHEMA_PATH="${ZEROCLAW_SCHEMA_PATH:-/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs}"
export ZEROCLAW_UNIX_SOCKET="${ZEROCLAW_UNIX_SOCKET:-/run/ghostbridge/container.sock}"
export GHOSTBRIDGE_SOCKET_UID="${GHOSTBRIDGE_SOCKET_UID:-1000000}"
export GHOSTBRIDGE_SOCKET_GID="${GHOSTBRIDGE_SOCKET_GID:-1000000}"
export GHOSTBRIDGE_SOCKET_MODE="${GHOSTBRIDGE_SOCKET_MODE:-0660}"
export RUST_LOG="${RUST_LOG:-op_grpc_bridge=info,info}"

exec /usr/local/bin/op-grpc-bridge-zeroclaw

#!/bin/bash
# Install and configure all op-dbus systemd services
set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
SYSTEMD_DIR="$SCRIPT_DIR/systemd"
PROJECT_ROOT="$(dirname "$SCRIPT_DIR")"

echo "=== Installing Op-DBus Systemd Services ==="

# Check if running as root or with sudo
if [[ $EUID -ne 0 ]]; then
    echo "This script requires root privileges. Using sudo..."
    exec sudo "$0" "$@"
fi

# Copy all service files
echo "Copying service files to /etc/systemd/system/..."
cp "$SYSTEMD_DIR/op-web.service" /etc/systemd/system/
cp "$SYSTEMD_DIR/op-mcp.service" /etc/systemd/system/
cp "$SYSTEMD_DIR/op-mcp-server.service" /etc/systemd/system/ 2>/dev/null || true
cp "$SYSTEMD_DIR/op-web-hf.service" /etc/systemd/system/
cp "$SYSTEMD_DIR/op-agents.service" /etc/systemd/system/
cp "$SYSTEMD_DIR/op-agent@.service" /etc/systemd/system/
cp "$SYSTEMD_DIR/op-dbus.target" /etc/systemd/system/
cp "$SYSTEMD_DIR/op-dbus-all.service" /etc/systemd/system/

# Reload systemd
echo "Reloading systemd daemon..."
systemctl daemon-reload

# Enable core services
echo "Enabling core services..."
systemctl enable op-web.service
systemctl enable op-mcp.service
systemctl enable op-dbus-all.service

echo ""
echo "=== Installation Complete ==="
echo ""
echo "Available commands:"
echo "  Start all:     sudo systemctl start op-dbus-all"
echo "  Stop all:      sudo systemctl stop op-dbus-all"

echo "  op-agents      - Agent services"

1	#!/bin/bash
2	# deploy/deploy.sh — Operation D-Bus system deployment (s6-rc)
3	#
4	# Usage:
5	#   sudo ./deploy/deploy.sh [--skip-network] [SERVICE|all]
6	#
7	# Services: op-dbus, op-web-server, op-chat, op-services, op-projection,
8	# op-dbus-mirror, op-grpc-bridge, op-mcp-compact
9	
10	set -euo pipefail
11	
12	PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
13	DEPLOY_DIR="${PROJECT_ROOT}/deploy"
14	INSTALL_BIN="/usr/local/bin"
15	S6_SV="/etc/s6/sv"
16	S6_DB="/etc/s6/db"
17	
18	SERVICES=(
19	    "op-identity:op-identity-sled:opdbus"
20	    "op-web:op-dbus:op-dbus"
21	    "op-web:op-web-server:op-web-server"
22	    "op-chat:op-chat:chatmanager"
23	    "op-dbus-mirror:ovs-dbus-init:op-dbus-mirror"
24	    "op-projection:projection_server:op-projection"
25	    "op-grpc-bridge:op-grpc-bridge-zeroclaw:op-grpc-bridge-zeroclaw"
26	    "op-mcp:op-mcp-server:op-mcp-compact"
27	    "op-cognitive-mcp:op-cognitive-mcp:op-cognitive-mcp"
28	    # Blob gemma4+zeroclaw complete deployments are handled by btrfs subvols + helpers (see docs/BLOB_ARCHITECTURE_SYNTHESIS.md + crate op-projection/src/blob.rs)
29	#   Example: btrfs subvol create /mnt/btrfs-root/@blob-zeroclaw-gemma4 ; mount ... ; materialize the PluginObjectBlob there.
30	)
31	
32	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
33	# Args
34	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
35	
36	SKIP_NETWORK=false
37	TARGET=""
38	
39	for arg in "$@"; do
40	    case "$arg" in
41	        --skip-network) SKIP_NETWORK=true ;;
42	        --help) echo "Usage: sudo $0 [--skip-network] [SERVICE|all]"; exit 0 ;;
43	        -*) echo "Unknown flag: $arg" >&2; exit 1 ;;
44	        *) TARGET="$arg" ;;
45	    esac
46	done
47	
48	[[ "$EUID" -eq 0 ]] || { echo "Run with sudo." >&2; exit 1; }
49	
50	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
51	# Logging
52	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
53	
54	log()   { echo -e "\033[0;32m[DEPLOY]\033[0m $*"; }
55	warn()  { echo -e "\033[1;33m[WARN]\033[0m $*"; }
56	error() { echo -e "\033[0;31m[ERROR]\033[0m $*"; exit 1; }
57	
58	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
59	# Helpers
60	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
61	
62	append_env_if_missing() {
63	    local file="$1" key="$2" value="$3"
64	    grep -q "^${key}=" "$file" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$value" >> "$file"
65	}
66	
67	s6_restart() {
68	    local svc="$1"
69	    if [[ -d "/run/service/${svc}" ]]; then
70	        s6-svc -r "/run/service/${svc}" && log "Restarted s6 service: ${svc}"
71	    else
72	        warn "s6 service not running: ${svc}"
73	    fi
74	}
75	
76	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
77	# STEP 1: System files
78	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
79	
80	install_system_files() {
81	    log "Installing system files..."
82	
83	    # D-Bus policy
84	    install -d /etc/dbus-1/system.d
85	    install -m 0644 "${DEPLOY_DIR}/dbus/org.opdbus.conf"  /etc/dbus-1/system.d/org.opdbus.conf
86	    install -m 0644 "${DEPLOY_DIR}/dbus/org.dbusmcp.conf" /etc/dbus-1/system.d/org.dbusmcp.conf
87	    dbus-send --system --type=method_call \
88	        --dest=org.freedesktop.DBus /org/freedesktop/DBus \
89	        org.freedesktop.DBus.ReloadConfig 2>/dev/null || true
90	    log "Installed D-Bus policy"
91	
92	    # s6 service definitions
93	    for svc_dir in "${DEPLOY_DIR}/s6"/*/; do
94	        svc="$(basename "$svc_dir")"
95	        if [ ! -f "${svc_dir}/type" ]; then
96	            continue
97	        fi
98	        install -d "${S6_SV}/${svc}"
99	        if [[ "$(readlink -f "$svc_dir")" != "$(readlink -f "${S6_SV}/${svc}")" ]]; then
100	            cp -a "${svc_dir}/." "${S6_SV}/${svc}/"
101	        fi
102	        chmod 0755 "${S6_SV}/${svc}/run" 2>/dev/null || true
103	        chmod 0755 "${S6_SV}/${svc}/up" 2>/dev/null || true
104	        chmod 0755 "${S6_SV}/${svc}/shell_up" 2>/dev/null || true
105	        log "Installed s6 service: ${svc}"
106	    done
107	
108	    # systemd-networkd units
109	    if [[ -d "${DEPLOY_DIR}/systemd/networkd" ]]; then
110	        install -d /etc/systemd/network
111	        find "${DEPLOY_DIR}/systemd/networkd" -maxdepth 1 -type f | while read -r f; do
112	            install -m 0644 "$f" "/etc/systemd/network/$(basename "$f")"
113	        done
114	        log "Installed systemd-networkd units"
115	    fi
116	
117	    # Netplan
118	    install -d /etc/netplan
119	    install -m 0600 "${DEPLOY_DIR}/netplan/01-ovsbr0.yaml" /etc/netplan/01-ovsbr0.yaml
120	    log "Installed /etc/netplan/01-ovsbr0.yaml"
121	
122	    # wgcf — never overwrite the live key
123	    if [[ -f /etc/wireguard/wgcf.conf ]]; then
124	        log "/etc/wireguard/wgcf.conf present — not overwriting"
125	    else
126	        warn "/etc/wireguard/wgcf.conf not found. Skipping WARP checks."
127	    fi
128	
129	    # App environment
130	    install -d /etc/op-dbus
131	    if [[ ! -f /etc/op-dbus/environment ]]; then
132	        install -m 0640 "${DEPLOY_DIR}/environment.default" /etc/op-dbus/environment
133	        log "Installed /etc/op-dbus/environment"
134	    else
135	        # Merge: add keys from default that aren't already present
136	        while IFS= read -r line; do
137	            [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
138	            [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
139	            key="${line%%=*}"
140	            grep -q "^${key}=" /etc/op-dbus/environment 2>/dev/null \
141	                || { echo "$line" >> /etc/op-dbus/environment; log "Added ${key} to environment"; }
142	        done < "${DEPLOY_DIR}/environment.default"
143	    fi
144	
145	    # Ensure runtime dirs exist
146	    local state_dir
147	    state_dir="$(awk -F= '$1=="OP_DBUS_STATE_DIR"{print $2;exit}' /etc/op-dbus/environment)"
148	    state_dir="${state_dir:-/var/lib/op-dbus}"
149	    install -d -m 0750 "${state_dir}/cache" /run/op-dbus
150	    append_env_if_missing /etc/op-dbus/environment "OP_DBUS_CACHE_DIR" "${state_dir}/cache"
151	
152	    log "System files installed."
153	}
154	
155	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
156	# STEP 2: Network bootstrap
157	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
158	
159	run_network_bootstrap() {
160	    [[ "$SKIP_NETWORK" == "true" ]] && { log "Skipping network bootstrap."; return 0; }
161	    local script="${DEPLOY_DIR}/deploy-network.sh"
162	    [[ -x "$script" ]] || error "${script} not found or not executable"
163	    log "Running network bootstrap..."
164	    "$script"
165	}
166	
167	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
168	# STEP 3: Build + install service binaries
169	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
170	
171	build_and_install() {
172	    local crate="$1" binary="$2"
173	    log "Building ${binary}..."
174	    cargo build --release -p "$crate" --bin "$binary" \
175	        || error "Build failed: ${binary}"
176	    install -m 0755 "${PROJECT_ROOT}/target/release/${binary}" "${INSTALL_BIN}/${binary}"
177	    log "Installed ${binary} → ${INSTALL_BIN}/${binary}"
178	}
179	
180	deploy_service() {
181	    local crate="$1" binary="$2" service="$3"
182	    build_and_install "$crate" "$binary"
183	    s6_restart "$service"
184	    log "✅ ${service} deployed"
185	}
186	
187	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
188	# Main
189	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
190	
191	command -v cargo >/dev/null || warn "cargo not found — service builds will fail"
192	command -v s6-svc >/dev/null || warn "s6-svc not found"
193	
194	install_system_files
195	run_network_bootstrap
196	
197	for entry in "${SERVICES[@]}"; do
198	    IFS=':' read -r crate binary service <<< "$entry"
199	    if [[ -z "$TARGET" || "$TARGET" == "all" || "$TARGET" == "$service" || "$TARGET" == "$crate" ]]; then
200	        deploy_service "$crate" "$binary" "$service"
201	    fi
202	done
203	
204	log "Deployment complete."
205
